rows.name: Start the Foreman's session
means: `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` with `initiation: "user_asked"`, `title: "<title>"`, `context: "fresh"`, no `cwd`, no `preset`, `use_worktree: false`.
`model: "claude-sonnet-5-5"`, `effort: "medium"`, the user's permission mode; leave the session linked.

rows.name: Own session id and title
means: `get_session("self")` gives the session's id and title.
The transcript's id is `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`.

rows.name: Set a session's own title
means: `set_session_title` renames the session itself (the Chief of Staff, a Griller, the Foreman).
`get_session("self")` shows the new title.

rows.name: The skills
means: `/chantier:chantier` (the router), `/chantier:chief-of-staff [foreman|direct]`, `/chantier:griller`, `/chantier:status`.
A plugin's `skills/<name>/` is `/<plugin>:<name>`; the argument `reload` of the router and of both role skills reloads the rules.

rows.name: Load another skill (the router)
means: The host's Skill tool loads another skill.
The router (`/chantier:chantier`) asks which role, then loads that role's skill.

rows.name: List the sessions and their state
means: The session tools of the `mcp__ccd_session__` set list the sessions and tell whether the seat's session is alive.
The exact tool and its states are not recorded on this host; the "looks stopped" line of `session-start.md` is asked.

rows.name: Message another session of the user
means: `SendMessage` to the other session's id (a hand-over, a Griller's line).
Claude Desktop limits messages between sessions; a refused send is reported, never sent another way.

rows.name: A session's link (for the seat)
means: `get_session` gives the session's link; the seat records it.
The name of the link field is not recorded on this host.

rows.name: Start a Driver or a worker
means: `Agent` with `subagent_type: chantier:<role>`; `run_in_background: true` for a Driver.
The `model` parameter only when `$CHANTIER` printed a start value (an alias), as printed; no effort.

rows.name: Models at an agent's start
means: A named agent starts with a model through the `model` parameter of `Agent`, set to an alias: `opus`, `sonnet` or `haiku`.
The CLI maps the identifier to the alias: `claude-opus-5-5` is `opus`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` is `sonnet`, `claude-haiku-5-5` is `haiku`.
The full identifier is not recorded as accepted; the agent's tools stay unchanged.

rows.name: Start a generic agent
means: Not on this host as a separate start: a configured model goes through the `model` parameter of `Agent` (see `model-at-start`).
The role runs as its named agent `chantier:<role>` with that model, its tools unchanged.

rows.name: The model a role ran on
means: Not recorded on this host: no step reads the model back after a start.
The model a role ran on is the one its transcript shows.

rows.name: Start the Spec-writer
means: `Agent` with `run_in_background: true` and `subagent_type: chantier:spec-writer`; no effort.
The `model` parameter as in `start-driver`, only when `$CHANTIER playbook` printed one.

rows.name: Start the Spec critic
means: `Agent` with `run_in_background: true` and `subagent_type: chantier:spec-critic`; no effort.
The `model` parameter only when `$CHANTIER playbook` printed one or the user asked for Fable.

rows.name: Start the Retro critic
means: `Agent` with `subagent_type: chantier:retro-critic`; no effort.
The `model` parameter only when `$CHANTIER playbook` printed one or the user asked for Fable.

rows.name: Message a Driver
means: `SendMessage` to the Driver's agent id.
A Driver that stopped resumes, with its context, when it gets the message (see `resume-subagent`).

rows.name: Message the Chief of Staff
means: `SendMessage` to the Chief of Staff's session id.
The Foreman's lines and a Griller's `ready` line travel the same way.

rows.name: A Driver's final report to a Foreman's Desktop session
means: For a steering session of Claude Desktop (id `local_…`), a Driver sends one message: its final report, by `SubagentHandback`, at its end.
Before its end a background subagent has no means to reach that session, and `SendMessage` to `main` does not reach it.
The report's first line is the hand-back line, then every other line due (`anomaly`, `push`), one per line, as the cards word them.
An `anomaly` is recorded when it happens: `$CHANTIER note <cr> "anomaly: <text>"`.

rows.name: A Driver messages its steering session in direct mode
means: Direct mode run from Claude Desktop: the final report only, as `driver-hand-back` says, once, at the Driver's end.
Direct mode run from a terminal or VS Code: `SendMessage` to `main`, and the `Steering:` line names it.

rows.name: Stop a Driver
means: `TaskStop` with the Driver's agent id.
After a Driver's own `TaskStop` with no restart at once, the steering session clears the recorded id.

rows.name: Stop an ended Driver that wakes again
means: `TaskStop` with the Driver's agent id, as in `stop-driver`.
Whether it also ends the background tasks that Driver left running is not known: say so, never tell it as a fact.

rows.name: A CR Driver's start folder
means: A CR Driver starts in the folder the plugin's mod gives it, as `write-guard` says.
That is its worktree, or the project's root while the worktree does not exist yet.

rows.name: Stop a background task of one's own
means: `TaskStop` with the id the start returned (`Bash` or `PowerShell` with `run_in_background: true`, or `Monitor`).
The Driver agents list `TaskStop` in their tools for it.

rows.name: Name the holders of the checkout's environment
means: Windows, the `PowerShell` tool: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` filtered on an `ExecutablePath` under `<plugin root>\.venv\`, showing PIDs and `CommandLine`.
macOS and Linux, the `Bash` tool: `ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep -F "<plugin root>/.venv/"`, the grep line itself excluded.
A `chantier.exe` and its child `python.exe` are one holder, named by the top process's PID, subcommand and `--project` value.
Read-only: never `Stop-Process`, `taskkill` or `kill` on a holder.

rows.name: Stop another session
means: `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__stop_session` with the session's id (a Foreman not answering, on the user's yes).
Whether it works from Remote Control is not recorded on this host.

rows.name: Agent ids of the project
means: The `name:` of a file in `.claude/agents/` or `~/.claude/agents/`.
The plugin's own agents are `chantier:<role>`.

rows.name: Models
means: The Spec-writer, the Spec critic and the Retro critic run Opus 5.5; the Foreman, every Driver and the workers run Sonnet 5.5.
Unless the configuration (`hosts.<host>.roles`) sets one; the defaults are `config/chantier.defaults.yml`'s.
A task under escalation runs the role's `escalation` model, printed by `$CHANTIER playbook` (`coder`, `debugger`, `conflict-resolver`).

rows.name: Skills and tools of a session
means: Not recorded on this host: how a session lists its skills and tools, and whether a subagent sees what the session sees.
The Chief of Staff compares a role's needs with what it can tell.

rows.name: Preflight P2
means: `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` loads.
Preflight P2 passes when that tool is available to the session.

rows.name: Ask the user a series of questions
means: The host's question tool (`AskUserQuestion`): at most 4 questions per call, at most 4 options per question, plus its own free answer ("Other").
The reference opens each question's text; the tool's short header field, if used, need not hold it.
Remote Control relays the same tool: the same 4-question form shows on the phone, above the conversation.
The text is written before every call all the same.

rows.name: Run the board
means: `Bash` with `run_in_background: true` and the command `$CHANTIER serve --seat <id>`; `$CHANTIER serve --restart --seat <id>` runs the same way.
Add `--forge-always` on a host that cannot run the watcher.
Read its first lines from the background task's output; stop it with the host's stop of a background shell.

rows.name: The board's Griller
means: The surface server starts `claude -p` with the JSON output, as the agent `chantier:board-griller` with `--model <effective model>`.
The conversation is fixed by an id and resumed by it; the prompt goes on standard input; no user, project or local settings load; the plugin loads explicitly.
The run works from an allow list alone (the Griller card's "Started from the board"); the exact flags are not recorded on this host.

rows.name: Trust of a workspace inside a trusted folder
means: A folder the user trusted once in Claude Desktop at the desk covers every new folder created inside it later.
A session started on such a folder from Remote Control does not ask for trust.

rows.name: Move a started session to another folder
means: A session started with no `cwd` may move with `mcp__ccd_directory__change_directory` into a folder inside a trusted folder.
No question is asked in auto mode and the next turn runs there; project instructions do not reload (the session keeps its own `AGENTS.md`).
`clear_session` on another id is denied by the auto mode classifier; no chantier route uses it.

rows.name: Prompt cache TTL
means: A session's cache writes are 1-hour (`cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` in its transcript's usage).
A subagent's cache writes are 5-minute (`ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`).

rows.name: Steering wake bound (60 minutes)
means: The CLI refuses a `steering_wake` over 60 minutes.
The shipped default is 55 minutes (3300 seconds), scheduled with `ScheduleWakeup`.

rows.name: Heartbeat
means: The steering session runs the `/loop` skill in dynamic mode; its prompt is `chantier status --refresh --batch <batch> --epoch <n>` alone, with no interval.
Each wake is scheduled with `ScheduleWakeup`, the steering wake of the `timing: Claude Code session:` line `chantier playbook` prints, in seconds.
It ends with `ScheduleWakeup` `stop: true`, after `chantier status --stop-heartbeat --batch <batch> --epoch <n>`; it never ends the session.
An order's line or a `ping` starts a turn; if a Driver is left running, the heartbeat is armed again.

rows.name: Run the watcher
means: `Monitor`, with no timeout, running the command the `watch: not running` or `still running` line prints, as is (it ends with `--stream`).
Each notification (event lines closed by `... still watching`) and the monitor's end start a turn of the idle session.
On the `no event for <name> in 2 h` line, start again at once as printed, nothing told.
Auto mode drops every `Monitor` allow rule, so the start is the classifier's call.

rows.name: The watcher when the session ends
means: Not recorded on this host: whether the host ends a background command when the session ends.
An orphaned watcher ends by the CLI's own rules: when the project's seat is another session's, or after 2 h with no event and no batch in flight.

rows.name: The board when the session ends
means: Not recorded on this host: whether the host ends a background command when the session ends.
The board stops when the seat moves (the CLI); a board a watcher started stops 30 minutes after its last client.

rows.name: Limit on messages
means: Claude Desktop limits messages between sessions: 10 since someone last typed.
A refused send is reported, never sent another way; the limit applies to the lines between a Griller and the Chief of Staff, and to a hand-over's.

rows.name: End a subagent's turn with nothing running in the background
means: The host asks a subagent for its hand-back at once (`[handback-send-enforce] Your report has not been delivered. Call SubagentHandback…`).
It asks before a resumed worker's reply arrives; a background shell's end wakes the subagent (the CI wait of `driver.md`).

rows.name: A background subagent stops
means: `<task-notification>` summary `Agent "<name>" is waiting on its own background work`: it stopped with its own work running and resumes when that reports.
`Agent "<name>" finished`: it stopped with no live background child, and its `SubagentHandback` report arrives as a message.

rows.name: A background subagent is stopped from outside
means: The steering transcript's `attachment` record `task_status` with `status: "killed"` and the agent's id as `taskId`, seen as `Task "<name>" (<id>) was stopped.`
A message to the stopped agent is refused. What a stop by the user in the app leaves in the transcript is not recorded.

rows.name: Resume a stopped subagent
means: `SendMessage` to a stopped subagent's agent id resumes it with its context.
Not for a subagent the host stopped (`task_status` `killed`): the message gets `Agent <id> was stopped and won't be resumed. Treat its work as cancelled; ...`.
A refused agent answers a `taken back:` or `record your hand-back` note with its refusal.

rows.name: Compacting
means: `/compact` continues the same conversation; connected devices follow it, `$CHANTIER cost` keeps the transcript, and `/clear` may replace it.
No role runs it: the person types it. The window is `autoCompactWindow` (100000 to 1000000), capped at the model's context window.
`idleCompaction` (default true) compacts after about an hour idle; `/autocompact` and the setting set the window.

rows.name: Reload after a compaction
means: The plugin's mod hooks `session.compact`: after each compaction of a session that loaded a chantier role skill, it adds one reload message.
The message tells the role to call its chantier skill again with the argument `reload`; the answer opens with one line saying the rules were reloaded.
It leaves a subagent's own compaction alone and never vetoes one; the manual reload (`/chantier:chantier reload`) works everywhere.

rows.name: The write guard
means: The plugin's mod reads the `writes: <folder>; <folder>` line of a spawn's prompt and starts the agent in the first folder (a `worktree:` line wins).
That agent's Write, Edit or NotebookEdit outside every folder is refused: `refused: <path> is outside the folders this agent may write in (...); write there`.
Its shell writes (`>`, `tee`, `sed -i`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `Set-Content`, `Out-File`) follow the same rule; `git`, `gh`, `glab` and the chantier CLI pass.
Not guarded: the main session, the Release, stack and QA drivers, the Spec agents, the Griller, the Demo explorer, any agent with no `writes:` line.

rows.name: A Griller in a worktree
means: A Griller in a worktree sends its files by `SendMessage` to the seat's session, naming the absolute paths.
The Chief of Staff on the main checkout reads them under `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`.

rows.name: A session in a planning surface writing in the project's clone
means: A session in a planning surface writes the planning folder by absolute paths, and the project's clone and worktrees outside its own folder.
The host must allow those folders: add the clone and its worktrees folder as working directories (`/add-dir <path>`, or `additionalDirectories`).
